source_packet.selected_slice: Does a material change in a UCITS fund investment objective, policy or restriction require prior SFC approval under this circular, taking account of product features, home requirements and the application transition?

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

question.question: Within the circular’s defined UCITS and material post-authorisation investment-change scope, does the identified change qualify for item (ii)’s removal of prior SFC approval under the proposed commencement and transition assumptions?
question.unit_of_assessment: One identified material post-authorisation change to an investment objective, policy or restriction, assessed as a whole, for a fund meeting the quoted circular-specific UCITS definition, together with its application history.
question.actor: The fund within the circular’s defined UCITS class seeking removal of SFC prior approval.
question.temporal_basis: On or after 28 November 2025 is a result condition. Application receipt before that date and absence of approval or authorisation at that date jointly establish the proposed legacy exclusion.
question.true_means: The in-scope change meets home requirements, involves no novel or complex product features or possible local policy implications, satisfies commencement, and has no preserved pre-effective pending application. No separate home-supervision condition is imposed. Notification, filing, post-vetting and overall compliance are not decided.
question.false_means: Within scope, this removal is unavailable under the proposed reading; approval is not thereby necessarily required and non-compliance is not established. A fund or change outside scope receives no determination. Unknown facts remain unknown.

question.question: For a covered material post-authorisation investment change assessed after commencement and outside the legacy-application transition, are the home-compliance and exception conditions for removal of prior SFC approval satisfied?

question.actor: The covered UCITS fund seeking removal of SFC prior approval outside the legacy-application transition.
question.temporal_basis: Scope requires an assessment date on or after 28 November 2025 and excludes applications received before that date that remained without approval or authorisation at that date. The assessment date does not establish a universal implementation-date test.
question.true_means: Within scope, the change complies with applicable home requirements and involves neither novel nor complex product features nor possible local policy implications. It therefore meets the stated removal conditions, without determining overall compliance.
question.false_means: Within scope, home compliance or absence of an exception fails, so this removal is unavailable. This does not establish a prohibition, non-compliance or the complete underlying approval obligation. Pre-effective assessments and legacy pending applications are outside scope, not false results. Unknown facts remain unknown.

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.

source_packet.selected_slice: Does a material change in a UCITS fund investment objective, policy or restriction require prior SFC approval under this circular, taking account of product features, home requirements and the application transition?

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Implementation
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
Obligation of management companies

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
2 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/faqs/Publicly-offered-investment-products
3 Please refer to https://www.sfc.hk/en/Forms/products/Investment-products-Forms-and-checklists
